bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Selloff: Worst Tech Drawdown in Years as Capex/ROI Debate Peaks
bullets.body: The week saw a violent unwind in AI/hyperscaler exposures — SOX fell 6.7-9.5% (worst stretch in 20+ years), NDX lost 2.6-2.9% on its worst single day since June, and the AI Tech basket dropped 4.3-8.25% w/w. GS reported global Info Tech saw the largest 2-week net selling on record (-3.3 SD); hedge fund net exposure to AI infrastructure collapsed from ~35-47% overweight to near equal-weight. META fell 9.4% after disclosing 'hundreds of billions' in multi-year AI financing needs and negative FCF (-$2.1B in Q3 on $34.9B capex), while its 5-year CDS hit a record 119bps. The core debate: AI capex-to-revenue ratios are rising and monetization timelines remain unclear, with hyperscaler NTM EPS estimates plateauing since August.

bullets.title: Rotation Away from AI/Growth Into Value, SMIDs, Defensives — Not a Liquidation
bullets.body: Equal-weight S&P outperformed the cap-weighted index by ~160bps on the week; Russell 2000 gained 2.0% vs Nasdaq -0.71%. JPM characterized the move as 'painful under the surface but not a liquidation' — hedge fund alpha hit -2.9% (worst since Feb 2021) but CTAs were the primary sellers, retail buying hit 5th percentile on 20-day basis, and multi-strat de-grossing slowed sharply. XLP (Staples) outperformed QQQs by +14.5% over the prior 10 days — widest spread outside crisis periods. Software (IGV) gained +5.73-6.0% as defensive tech while semis cratered. Healthcare (XLV) hit all-time highs, up 7.7% in October.

bullets.title: 10-Year Treasury at 5.00%, Yield Curve Flattening as AI Capex Lifts Neutral Rate Expectations
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield held at 5.00% (up 3bps on Friday), with the 2-year at 4.68%. JPM technical analysis identified S&P 500 7,500-7,600 support as the key level for the Treasury rally to extend meaningfully beyond 4.75% resistance. Multiple sources flagged AI capital demand as large enough to structurally lift r-star globally, while the long end (20s/30s) signaled credit event risk into the AI bubble. Bund yields hit 3.34% (highest since 2011); French 10-year OAT crossed 5% (24-year high) with spreads near 180bps vs Bunds, approaching GFC-era levels amid social unrest.

bullets.title: WTI Crude Above $100, Brent at $114-116 on US-Iran Escalation; $20 Geopolitical Risk Premium
bullets.body: WTI crude surged 4.3% on the week (third straight weekly gain) to settle above $100/bbl, while Brent advanced 5.8% to ~$116. JPM estimated Brent fair value at ~$94/bbl, implying a ~$20 geopolitical risk premium from Iran-related escalation concerns. Multiple sources noted US-Israel reportedly planning intensive operations, Houthi attacks on Saudi targets, and mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Energy sector gained 2.51% on the week. Oil's technical target is cited by some analysts at $120. The energy sector is up +55% YTD vs tech +21%, and is broadly favored as underinvested with constrained supply.

bullets.title: FOMC Wednesday Expected to Hold; December Hike Probability at 80-88%
bullets.body: The FOMC meeting on Wednesday October 28 is expected to leave rates unchanged (~90% market probability for hold). Fed-funds futures show 80-88% probability of a hike at the December meeting. Multiple sources note the Fed is slow to react to AI capex uncertainty as long as inflation remains above 2%, growth exceeds trend, and 2027 capex plans are intact — all three conditions currently hold. October flash PMIs came in strong: manufacturing 56.0 (above 55.5 consensus), services 57.9 near consensus; selling prices rose at the fastest pace since August 2022.

bullets.title: Hedge Fund Positioning Washed Out: Net Leverage at Multi-Year Lows, Shorts Near 5-Year Highs
bullets.body: GS Prime: overall gross leverage hit 312.3% (79th percentile 1-year, 96th 5-year), net leverage fell to 71.8% (3rd percentile 1-year). Fundamental L/S net leverage at 47% (1st percentile 3-year). October 22 was the 5th largest single-day de-grossing event of the year (-1.6 SD), driven entirely by long selling — largest since September 2025. TMT-focused funds were down 9.6% MTD, with >40% of US L/S funds now flat or negative YTD. AI/Tech positioning fell to 94th percentile from 99th but remains elevated. Short leverage is near 5-year highs, which GS sees as creating asymmetric upside potential.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler Earnings Next Week (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN) Are the Defining AI Monetization Test
bullets.body: 35% of SPY/QQQ market cap reports in the week of Oct 26-30, headlined by MSFT and GOOGL on Wednesday (same day as FOMC) and AMZN Thursday. Buyside bar for AWS is ~43-44% growth (vs consensus 37%); Azure expected +46-47% YoY. META's 4Q guide of $73-76B (midpoint +24.4% YoY) beat consensus. Key debates: META's 2027 capex ($225-250B vs consensus $201B), GOOGL's TPU business value, and whether MSFT will discontinue reporting Copilot seat additions. Jefferies and others note the Nasdaq vs Russell positioning gap is at the widest heading into any Mag7 earnings season since 2021.

bullets.title: $20B+ Systematic Selling Forecast Next Week; Levered ETF Rebalancing Hit $33B on Thursday
bullets.body: MS QDS forecasts ~$20B global equity supply from systematic sellers next week. Thursday saw $33B in equity supply from levered ETF rebalancing — the 3rd largest single day since 2010. Global macro systematic strategies are at the 70th 5-year percentile in leverage (North America at 94th). The momentum factor posted its worst single day in 3 years on Thursday (-7.7% for US L/S momentum), and MSZZMOMO is down 17% since the October 2 peak and 38% from its June high. CTA strategies have cut US equity exposure every day since October 13, concentrated in Nasdaq.

bullets.title: SpaceX Seeking 80K Cell Sites for Terrestrial Wireless Network; Tower REITs Rally 10%+
bullets.body: Reports emerged that SpaceX is in advanced talks with Crown Castle and other tower operators (AMT, SBAC) to access ~80,000 US cell sites for a fourth national wireless carrier, having already acquired 800MHz spectrum. CCI identified as prime beneficiary (US pureplay, ~40K pre-permitted sites); tower stocks rallied 8-10% while AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile fell 4-5%. Analysts estimate 80K leases could add $1.0-2.0B in incremental annual rent and 100-200bps to domestic organic growth. A full carrier build-out would cost $50-130B and potentially threaten traditional telcos.

bullets.title: CoreWeave Credit Stress: 2031 Notes at ~16% Yield; Needs $24-37B to Scale by YE27
bullets.body: CRWV's unsecured bond spreads have widened ~300bps since late August; its 2031 notes are yielding ~16%. MS estimates the company needs $24-37B in additional debt to reach 3.3GW compute capacity by year-end 2027 (from 1.85GW at YE26). Stock is down 30%+ over the past month. Multiple sources cite CRWV as the poster-child for AI debt concerns — concentrated OpenAI exposure, GPU depreciation risk, and near-zero equity value in bear scenarios. Credit markets have stopped funding the 'riskiest' parts of AI buildout while remaining accommodating to investment-grade hyperscalers.

bullets.title: France Sovereign Stress Escalates: OAT at 5% (24-Year High), Spreads at GFC Levels
bullets.body: French 10-year OAT yields crossed 5% for the first time since 2002 — a 24-year high — with OAT-Bund spreads near 180bps approaching GFC-era levels. France's CDS spreads rose 247% in 2026. JPM estimates social unrest will drag Q4 GDP by ~0.4-0.6% (annualized) with a 1Q27 payback; the government is sticking to its 5% deficit target. Moody's is reviewing the French rating for downgrade. Eurozone composite PMI fell 1.3pts to 51.9 in October, consistent with 1.5% annualized growth, but France fell to 48.4. ECB seen pausing in October with a December hike as near-certain.

bullets.title: UK Budget Next Week Seen as Fiscally Neutral; BoE November Hike Assured
bullets.body: The UK Autumn Budget is expected to be broadly fiscally neutral with modest tax rises (~£5bn), deferring major spending decisions to 2027. Fiscal headroom is estimated at ~£20bn (down from £24bn in spring). JPM revised UK CPI peak to 4.6% in Q1 2027 driven by energy bill increases. A November BoE rate hike is described as 'assured'; December hike unlikely absent second-round effects. UK consumer confidence collapsed 11 points to -24 in October — the largest decline since the pandemic. October flash PMI rose to 53.1, signaling ~1.6% annualized GDP growth.

bullets.title: US Housing Weakest Since 2012: NAHB at 29, Pending Sales Record Low, Starts Fall 5.2%
bullets.body: NAHB Housing Market Index fell to 29 in October — the lowest level since 2012. September housing starts fell 5.2% to 1.22M units (below 1.31M consensus), with both single-family (-4.6%) and multifamily (-6.7%) declining. Pending home sales fell a record 7.3% (vs -0.5% consensus). Mortgage rates are at 7.40-7.41%. Analysts note housing has effectively 'exited' the business cycle as an active growth contributor, with near-zero GDP impact from residential investment in Q3.

bullets.title: Q3 S&P 500 Earnings: 83% Beat Rate, 29.5% EPS Growth, but Surprise Magnitude Below Average
bullets.body: S&P 500 Q3 blended EPS growth is tracking 29.5% (near the 29.6% expected); 83% of reported companies beat EPS consensus — above the 82% one-year and 78% five-year averages. However, aggregate EPS beat by only 2.1% vs the 13.8% one-year average and 7.5% five-year average. Sales beat 66% of the time (below 77% one-year average). Energy sector leads at 135.6% EPS growth; TECH+ is at 47.9% though the Big 6 are lagging at 23.8% vs 29.7% for the rest of the market. 169 companies (~33.6% of S&P 500 market cap) report in the next 5 trading days.

bullets.title: ECB to Pause Next Week; December Hike Near-Certain; TPI Activation Very Unlikely Despite French Stress
bullets.body: The ECB is expected to hold rates at its October meeting, with a December hike viewed as 'almost certain' given inflation above target and elevated energy/gas prices. JPM forecasts additional hikes in December and March, with June hike risks. ECB explicitly views French government and presidential candidates as bearing responsibility for calming sovereign markets. Activation of the TPI (Transmission Protection Instrument) is considered 'very unlikely' — French spread widening is seen as helpful pressure on the political process. ECB will not slow QT given elevated inflation.

bullets.title: US Midterm Elections Approaching: Democrats Favored in House (88-92%) and Senate (60-68%)
bullets.body: Prediction markets have Democrats at 88-92% to win the House and 60-68% to win the Senate, with ~60% odds of unified Democratic control. Key market implications: defense spending capped near $1.15T, AI legislation punted (only 20% odds of passage), tariffs likely past peak with court challenges ongoing, and data center policy risk elevated in Texas and Ohio. Texas gubernatorial race (Abbott vs. Hinojosa) is the biggest data-center-specific risk given Texas holds ~26% of nationwide 2028-30 planned capacity. Morgan Stanley is hosting a post-ballots webcast on October 26.

bullets.title: Macro PMIs Strong But Input Prices Surging: Manufacturing Employment Highest Since 2012
bullets.body: October US flash manufacturing PMI edged higher to 56.0 (above 55.5 consensus); services PMI at 57.9. Manufacturing employment surged to its highest level since 2012. Input prices climbed faster than output prices in manufacturing (narrowing margins), while services input prices fell as output prices rose. Vendor delivery times lengthened, likely reflecting war-related supply-chain disruptions. Order backlogs climbed and inventories rose — consistent with strong headline activity. JPM October capex nowcaster holds at 0.8% globally.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO Expected by Thanksgiving at $1.5T+ Floor; OpenAI Raised $30B at $1.25T
bullets.body: Anthropic's S-1 is expected as early as next week with an IPO by Thanksgiving; valuation floor is now $1.5T+ (down from $2T+ expectations), based on OpenAI's $30B raise at $1.25T pre-money valuation. Multiple sources note Anthropic's H1 2026 operating losses were ~$80B while committing to ~$750B in compute spending over coming years. OpenAI's raise closed at $1.25T, below the $1.4T target. Neoclouds are heavily shorted and discounted but spot compute markets remain robust; compute futures launch from CFTC review is imminent and may provide price discovery on supply-demand imbalances.

bullets.title: META Equity Raise Expected Early 2027 via Non-Voting Class C Shares; $40B+ Size Discussed
bullets.body: META announced non-voting Class C shares effective January 19, 2027 — enabling capital raises without diluting Zuckerberg's voting control (Berkshire is a potential anchor). Multiple sources estimate the equity raise at $40B+ within weeks of the announcement. META's SEC filing describes 'hundreds of billions' in multi-year financing needs (equity + debt combined). California's Proposition 40 wealth tax creates a Zuckerberg stock sale overhang if passed. META's 2027 capex is estimated at $225-250B (consensus $201B), with Q3 FCF already negative at -$2.1B.

bullets.title: Agentic Commerce Emerging: WMT Launches Agent Gateway, Visa/BILL Pilot Live AI Payments
bullets.body: Walmart launched three agentic commerce tools (Agent Profiles, Walmart Agent Gateway, and agent permissions/controls), positioning itself alongside Meta Muse and Google Universal Cart as early leaders in AI-driven shopping. Analysts note large trusted retailers are structurally favored in agentic discovery — scale advantage reinforces incumbent dominance. Separately, Visa, BILL, and Billtrust completed the first live pilot enabling AI agents to initiate and complete B2B invoice payments end-to-end. Keybank estimates agents could facilitate ~10% of transactions by 2030; PayPal expects meaningful growth by 2028+. Consumer comfort remains limited (only 23% comfortable with agent-initiated purchases).
